finetune_permitted.note: Section 2.2: 'You may use, reproduce, modify, Distribute ... any of the HAI-DEF Services only in accordance with the terms'. Fine-tuned weights are 'Model Derivatives' (1.1(h)) and stay subject to the section 3.2 use restrictions and the Prohibited Use Policy.

redistribution.note: Section 3.1: redistribution of HAI-DEF or Model Derivatives requires (a) the section 3.2 use restrictions as an enforceable provision in any agreement governing use/distribution, and notifying recipients of them; (b) giving every recipient a copy of the Agreement; (c) seeking Health Regulatory Authorization when applicable; (d) prominent notices on modified files; (e) a 'Notice' text file with the prescribed HAI-DEF notice. The use restrictions (Prohibited Use Policy; no use that makes Google a medical-device 'manufacturer') flow down to every derivative. This limits the terms of an open-weight release: see Decisions needed.

rubric.selection_data: Preliminary fine-tune results on the project's own validation split only (patient-level split, proposal 3.4). Official test sets are never used to choose the base model.
hard_constraints: Open weights downloadable for local fine-tuning (no API-only access).
License permits fine-tuning, and either permits the intended open-weight release of the derivative or a human decision accepting the release terms is recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md.
Runs entirely on team-controlled machines for MIMIC data (PhysioNet rule, proposal 1.3.4).
Stage-3 LoRA fits 8x B200 per the estimate AND per the Tier-2 measured peak memory.
True parameter count is reported; a model is never relabelled to a different scale.

criteria.measure: Validation-split quality after the Tier-2/3 preliminary fine-tune (CXR findings macro-F1, CT report quality, department suggestion accuracy), same budget per candidate
Compatibility of the license with an open-weight release of the derivative (permissive > conditional > incompatible)
Tier-2 measured peak memory headroom and tokens/s on one B200
Base model zero-shot quality on the validation split before fine-tuning (proposal Table 3.2 comparator)
Closeness of the true parameter count to approximately 27B
transformers / peft / DeepSpeed / vLLM support without custom patches
Lower known or unknown overlap with evaluation sources scores higher

tie_breaks: Lower measured peak memory per GPU.
rubric.comparison_fairness: Every candidate gets the same data, token budget, LoRA rank grid, optimizer search budget and evaluation. Any exception is disclosed in the results.

decisions_needed.question: HAI-DEF section 3.1/3.2 require the use restrictions to flow down to any distributed derivative, plus notices, a copy of the terms and (when applicable) Health Regulatory Authorization. Does this allow the project's intended open-weight release? Must be settled before MedGemma can be the final base.
Lingshu-32B has 33,452,718,336 parameters. Does it count as 'approximately 27B' for the headline claim, or must any result be reported at its true scale?
Lingshu is MIT-licensed but built on Qwen2.5-VL (Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct is tagged apache-2.0). Confirm which notice obligations carry into a release of our derivative.

Both medical candidates were trained on MIMIC-CXR. Every base-vs-fine-tuned MIMIC-CXR comparison (proposal Table 3.2) must disclose this. Should MIMIC-CXR results for these bases be reported as contaminated?
